title: Lina's Family: Comparing and Measuring Length, Weight and Capacity
seo_title: Comparing and Measuring Length, Weight and Capacity Class 1 Worksheet with Answers (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 1, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 7: Lina's Family
standard_text: Measurement: comparing lengths, heights, weights and capacities using words such as longer, taller, heavier and holds more; measuring with non-standard units such as hand spans (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 1)
meta_desc: Class 1 Lina's Family worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 7): longer and shorter, taller, heavier and lighter, holds more, measuring with units. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Line things up at one end to compare length.
key_sub: Count the units with no gaps or overlaps.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Compare length and height: longer, shorter, taller.
  • Compare weight: heavier, lighter. Compare capacity: holds more, holds less.
  • Measure with the same unit (hand spans, clips) placed end to end.

Examples

Example

A pencil is 6 clips long and a crayon is 4 clips long. Which is longer?

6 is more than 4

Answer: The pencil

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not starting at the same lineLine up the ends before comparing.
Leaving gaps between unitsPlace units end to end.

faq.a: Things like hand spans, steps or paper clips used to measure before rulers.

faq.q: Why must units be the same size?
faq.a: So the count is fair: big and small clips give different numbers.

items.q: Put them in order from longest to shortest.
items.e: Find the longest first: the straw. Then the next: the pencil. Last is the shortest: the eraser. So the order is straw, pencil, eraser.

items.q: Put them in order from longest to shortest.
items.e: Find the longest first: the ribbon. Then the next: the crayon. Last is the shortest: the key. So the order is ribbon, crayon, key.

items.q: The rope is longer than the stick. The stick is longer than the pencil. Which is the longest?
items.e: The rope is longer than the stick, and the stick is longer than the pencil. So the order is rope, stick, pencil. The rope is the longest.

items.q: The bus is longer than the car. The car is longer than the bike. Which is the shortest?
items.e: The order from longest is bus, car, bike. The bike is the shortest.

items.q: The ribbon is shorter than the yarn. The yarn is shorter than the rope. Which is the longest?
items.e: Each one is shorter than the next. From shortest: ribbon, yarn, rope. So the rope is the longest. Read “shorter” carefully.

items.q: The cat is shorter than the dog. The dog is shorter than the horse. Which animal is in the middle?
items.e: From shortest to tallest: cat, dog, horse. The dog is in the middle.

items.q: Diya is taller than Arjun. Arjun is taller than Kabir. Who is the shortest?
items.e: Diya is taller than Arjun, and Arjun is taller than Kabir. From tallest: Diya, Arjun, Kabir. Kabir is the shortest.

items.q: Tara cannot move her desk to the door. She uses a string. The string is as long as the desk. The string is shorter than the door. Which is longer?
items.e: The string is the same length as the desk. The door is longer than the string, so the door is longer than the desk too. The door is longer.

items.q: Om has a string. It is as long as his book. The string is longer than his pencil. Which is longer, the book or the pencil?
items.e: The book and the string are the same length. The string is longer than the pencil. So the book is longer than the pencil.

items.q: The green snake is longer than the blue snake. The red snake is shorter than the blue snake. Which list goes from longest to shortest?
items.e: Green is longer than blue. Red is shorter than blue. So blue is in the middle: green, blue, red.

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the key?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the key to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: How many paper clips long is the eraser?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the eraser to the other: 1, 2. It is 2 paper clips long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the ribbon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the ribbon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: How long is the leaf?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the leaf to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: You measure a crayon with cubes. What do you count?
c: all the cubes in the box
items.e: Lay cubes along the crayon from end to end. Count only the cubes under the crayon. That number is its length.

items.q: How many cubes long is the straw?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the straw to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. It is 9 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the marker?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the marker to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the caterpillar to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cubes long. Touch each one as you count so you do not skip one or count one twice.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: Yes. The cubes start at one end of the pencil and go to the other end. They touch with no gaps and no overlaps. The pencil is 7 cubes long.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the crayon?
items.e: No, there are gaps between the paper clips. The empty spaces are not counted, so the number would be too small. Push the paper clips together so they touch.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the ribbon?
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. They lie on top of each other, so you would count too many. Lay them end to end, side by side.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the straw?
items.e: No, the start is wrong. The first cube does not start at the end of the straw. Line up the first one with the end of the straw.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the marker?
items.e: Yes. The paper clips start at one end of the marker and go to the other end. They touch with no gaps and no overlaps. The marker is 5 paper clips long.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the craft stick?
items.e: No, there are gaps between the cubes. The empty spaces are not counted, so the number would be too small. Push the cubes together so they touch.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the paper strip?
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. They lie on top of each other, so you would count too many. Lay them end to end, side by side.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: No, the start is wrong. The first paper clip sticks out before the pencil starts. Line up the first one with the end of the pencil.

items.q: Where should you put the first cube?
items.e: Put the first cube right at one end of the object. Then lay the next cubes end to end until you reach the other end.

items.q: What should you use to measure a pencil?
items.e: Every unit must be the same size. If some cubes are big and some are small, the count does not tell the length.
